story.head: The Maple Leafs pile it on the Blue Jackets
paras: Auston Matthews played his 700th NHL game. Jake Christiansen struck first for the Blue Jackets early in the first, but Kirill Marchenko made it 1-1 for Toronto on the power play midway through the period. The Maple Leafs’ Jake McCabe left in the first period and didn’t return. The second period was a wild one. William Nylander, Matthews and Easton Cowan scored three goals in less than five minutes early in the period to put the Leafs up 4-1. Jack Roslovic made it 5-1 later in the period. Columbus pulled Jet Greaves after five goals and turned to Cam Talbot for the rest of the second. Zack MacEwen and Erik Gudbranson dropped the gloves late in the second. Charlie Coyle cut Toronto’s lead to 5-2 early in the third. Marshall Rifai, undrafted and in his fifth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Morgan Rielly, with just over three minutes left to make it 6-2 for the Maple Leafs. Roslovic and Cowan each had a goal and two assists.

The Blue Jackets outshot the Maple Leafs 37-22, but the Maple Leafs’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Anthony Stolarz, who gave up five goals in Utah in his last start, made 35 saves for the Maple Leafs.
The Maple Leafs killed all six Blue Jackets power plays. The Maple Leafs moved to 5-4-2, and the Blue Jackets dropped to 3-5-0.

items.text: Charlie Coyle scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 11.
Nick Blankenburg was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Marshall Rifai played instead.
Two of the preview’s four calls held.
